breaking.headline: Stocks slide again as Nasdaq drops 1.7% ahead of Nvidia earnings
breaking.fact: The S&P 500 fell 1.21% to 7,470 and the Nasdaq 1.66% at midday Monday, with the VIX up to 21.02, as the AI selloff deepened; the November Empire State manufacturing index printed 7.8 against an 18 estimate, and Nvidia fell 3.9% ahead of Tuesday’s Q3 report, its first under interim CEO Colette Kress.

breaking.headline: Anthropic IPO order book now about 7x oversubscribed; closes Tuesday
breaking.fact: Orders for Anthropic’s IPO are now close to seven times the 825 million shares on offer, Bloomberg reported, up from about six times; the book closes Tuesday, pricing is Wednesday and trading starts Thursday as ANT. Up to 316 million shares could be sold by employees on the first day under the staged lockup, and the filing discloses about $900.9 billion in compute commitments.

breaking.headline: IEA says world oil market swings back to surplus in Q4
breaking.fact: The International Energy Agency reversed its deficit call Friday, saying world oil supply will average about 105 million barrels a day in the fourth quarter against demand, a surplus of roughly 1.7 million barrels a day, as Middle East exports recover faster than demand; Goldman Sachs sees the surplus swelling into 2027.

breaking.headline: Quad leaders to meet Tuesday in Manila, first summit of Trump’s second term
breaking.fact: Reuters reports the leaders of India, the U.S., Japan and Australia are expected to meet Tuesday in Manila, the first Quad leaders’ summit of President Trump’s second term; Washington dismissed reports the grouping is on “life support”. Trump arrives Tuesday, then flies to Shenzhen for APEC and Thursday’s meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.

weekInBrief.headline: ASEAN nations sign digital economy pact
weekInBrief.body: ASEAN nations signed the landmark Digital Economy Framework Agreement on Saturday, a pact meant to make it easier for businesses to trade online and reach customers across the region. The signing came as leaders gathered in Manila for the 49th ASEAN Summit, with the Philippines closing out its year as chair.

weekInBrief.headline: China warns tougher U.S. chip curbs could disrupt global supply chains
weekInBrief.body: China warned Monday that tougher U.S. chip curbs could disrupt global supply chains, as the AI hardware selloff spread from Taiwan to New York ahead of Nvidia’s earnings. The warning landed the same day Taiwan’s Taiex fell 6% and TSMC 5.7% on AI exposure fears.

weekInBrief.headline: Fed Chair Warsh speaks Monday as December hike bets top 93%
weekInBrief.body: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh speaks Monday as markets price a better than 93% chance of a 25-basis-point hike at the December meeting, the CME FedWatch tool shows, after hot October CPI and PPI readings. U.S. retail sales land Tuesday and the FOMC minutes Wednesday.

weekInBrief.headline: Bitcoin slides to lowest since July as crypto joins the selloff
weekInBrief.body: Bitcoin fell to its lowest level since July on Monday, near $64,000, as the crypto selloff ran alongside the slide in AI stocks; gold also eased, down about 0.6% to near $3,862 an ounce, extending last week’s losses.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Iran’s navy claimed two more tankers struck mines in the strait early Monday, bringing its claimed total to six tankers caught fire or sunk since Sunday — none of the claims independently verified — while its army said a third tanker caught fire east of the waterway in the past 24 hours. UKMTO verified a separate incident: an eastbound tanker hit by an unidentified projectile near Khasab, Oman, suffering an engine-room fire with no crew casualties. Tehran’s deputy foreign minister has floated a mediated two-day plan, via Qatar and Pakistan, to reopen the strait. On oil, the U.S. blockade still holds — Iranian crude is not getting out in any meaningful volume — while Reuters reported Monday that shipments of non-Iranian Gulf oil through the strait have nearly returned to pre-war levels.

space.headline: Booster explodes after aborted catch as Starship’s first orbital recovery sinks in
space.body: New detail from Monday’s account of Saturday’s Flight 15: the Super Heavy booster diverted to the Gulf after a low-fuel alarm, hovered briefly, then its flight termination system destroyed it — while Ship 42 completed 14 orbits over 22.5 hours, deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites and was caught by the tower’s arms on the first try. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman weighed in on the milestone, the National Space Society congratulated SpaceX, and SpaceX expects to begin launching Starships from Florida’s Kennedy Space Center within months.

space.headline: ULA Vulcan fails minutes after liftoff, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites
space.body: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket failed about 10 minutes after liftoff Sunday, destroying 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites. The failure is a setback for Amazon’s constellation buildout and a contrast with SpaceX, which caught a Starship upper stage returning from orbit on Saturday.

space.headline: Rubin Observatory spots dwarf planet candidate beyond Pluto
space.body: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has identified a distant object named 2026 ED138, a large, bright trans-Neptunian body now about 46 astronomical units from the Sun — beyond Pluto’s orbit. If confirmed as a dwarf planet it would join the five recognized by the International Astronomical Union, and it offers a new window on the solar system’s outer reaches.

space.headline: Self-illuminating fibers let soft robots show their movements — no batteries needed
space.body: Researchers led by DGIST in South Korea have built thin, tough fibers that emit light whenever a soft robot moves, giving an intuitive visual trace of its motion without batteries or complex circuits. The fibers survived stretching to more than twice their length and kept their light output after 1,000 stretch-release cycles; the work is published in Small Structures.

apod.title: The Last Ice on Puncak Jaya
apod.credit: NASA Earth Observatory images by Lauren Dauphin, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey; story by Kathryn Hansen — NASA Earth Observatory Image of the Day, November 16, 2026
apod.explanation: On the island of New Guinea, Indonesia’s Puncak Jaya once held glaciers year-round near the equator — but by September 2025 only about 0.09 square kilometers of ice remained, roughly 2 percent of the 1988 extent, in patches too small to flow like glaciers. This false-color Landsat 9 view from October 2026 shows the scattered remnants; an aerial survey planned for December should estimate what is left.
